request: Create a small, playable Bubble Break ASMR game for one player on desktop and touch. The player presses individual bubbles on a reusable bubble-wrap sheet. A press visibly depresses and pops that bubble with synchronized satisfying pop audio, then adds exactly one to the popped counter after the pop completes. Holding, spamming, or pressing a popped bubble must not count twice. Let the player finish a sheet of at least twelve bubbles, see completion feedback, and deliberately reset to a fresh sheet. Use a close, readable tabletop presentation and minimal counter/reset UI. Search Marketplace first for a complete reusable interaction, including any existing geometry, animation, sounds and behavior; inspect what it already provides and integrate only missing features. Search separately for missing media if needed. Audio must come from Marketplace and actually play. Record unavailable importer capabilities rather than pretending a suitable scripted component does not exist. Choose reasonable details yourself; no saving, multiplayer, purchases or large map. Success needs observed press/pop/recovery timing, per-bubble state, exact counting, sheet completion/reset and usable desktop/touch input. Do not claim success from code inspection alone.

spec.assetStrategy:
Begin with Marketplace Model discovery for a complete bubble-wrap popping interaction, because the requested asset may already supply geometry, per-bubble scripts, depression/pop/reset animation, embedded sound, input support, and completion behavior. Audit its exact hierarchy, source scripts, remote interfaces, dependencies, animation/media references, state ownership, and desktop/touch behavior before allocating replacement or glue scripts. Preserve all useful verified content and integrate only demonstrably missing counter, authoritative validation, completion, reset, lifecycle, camera, or HUD responsibilities.

Treat embedded pop sounds as media candidates with retained provenance, but still route them through native load, playback, and listening verification. If no relevant verified captured sound survives inspection, use the separate Audio need to search Marketplace. Audio is mandatory and has no procedural fallback.

The complete interactive Model is also mandatory for this Marketplace-first request. Unsupported source serialization, numeric requires, arbitrary HTTP behavior, missing dependencies, or importer inability to preserve its scripts/rigs are explicit review/capability gaps, not evidence that scripted Marketplace interactions do not exist and not permission to silently rebuild one. Exact integration script ownership remains intentionally undecided until inspection establishes what the retained component already owns. Scene composition may be authored around the retained component, but it must not replace uninspected Marketplace behavior or media.
spec.title: Bubble Break ASMR
spec.summary:
A compact, one-player tabletop experience centered on a reusable 4-by-3 bubble-wrap sheet. From spawn, the player immediately sees a close, angled view of the sheet on a small worktable, a restrained “0 / 12 popped” counter, and a reset control that is visually secondary until needed. Clicking or tapping an unpopped bubble begins one short, readable press phase: the dome depresses, a verified Marketplace pop sound plays at the visible pop moment, the bubble settles into its popped state, and only then the authoritative counter advances by exactly one. Locked per-bubble state prevents holds, repeated input, and concurrent requests from producing duplicate pops or counts. Popping all twelve bubbles produces concise sheet-complete feedback and enables a deliberate reset that restores every bubble and returns the count to zero.

The playable space is intentionally small: a safe spawn/viewing position faces one central table, the bubble sheet occupies the focal interaction area, and subtle tabletop edges and a compact backdrop bound the scene without creating travel or navigation overhead. Input is direct pointer/touch selection rather than avatar traversal. Server state owns bubble eligibility, action timing, completion, reset validation, and counting; the client owns pointer/touch input, close camera presentation, HUD rendering, and local visual responsiveness only where compatible with the inspected component.

Assumptions chosen as requested: twelve bubbles arranged in a readable 4-by-3 grid; a short press-pop-settle sequence of roughly a fraction of a second, with exact timing finalized after inspecting the retained Marketplace component; no persistence, purchases, upgrades, multiplayer competition, or large environment. Marketplace discovery and source/media inspection must occur before implementation ownership is finalized. If a suitable scripted component cannot be preserved because of importer or serialization limitations, that capability gap is reported rather than treated as permission to replace it procedurally. Completion requires native desktop and touch playtests with observed animation, audible playback, authoritative counting, completion, and reset behavior—not code inspection alone.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a close, calm ASMR tabletop composition with the bubble sheet as the dominant focal point. The sheet should read as a soft translucent or lightly tinted rectangular membrane with twelve clearly separated rounded domes, arranged in a regular 4-by-3 rhythm and large enough for reliable touch selection. Preserve verified Marketplace geometry, materials, animation, and media where available instead of restyling away useful authored detail.

Build the table from warm, low-saturation wood or neutral laminate tones, contrasted by a cool pale-blue or clear bubble sheet. Use rounded edges, broad simple shapes, and a restrained cream/charcoal interface palette. Keep background elements sparse and low contrast so every unpopped dome silhouette remains legible. A soft key light and mild fill should reveal dome curvature and depression without glare obscuring selection. The table surface, sheet border, and backdrop provide three clear depth layers; no unrelated props should compete with the interaction.

The close camera should frame the entire sheet with modest perspective, enough margin for pressed-bubble movement, and no bubble hidden behind the avatar. Desktop input receives a precise hover/press indication where the retained component permits it; touch targets remain comfortably separated and do not depend on hover. During a valid press, the selected dome visibly compresses before or at the audible pop, then settles into a clearly flatter popped silhouette. Invalid repeated presses produce no second pop, no second animation cycle, and no counter increment.

The HUD should contain only a compact counter and reset control inside a ScreenGui. Place the counter near a screen corner without covering the sheet; show an explicit fraction such as “Popped 7 / 12.” Completion feedback may use a brief centered message and gentle scale/fade treatment, while avoiding reward showers or noisy effects that conflict with the ASMR tone. The reset control must require a distinct click/tap and remain usable on both desktop and touch. Reset should visibly restore the complete sheet in a coordinated recovery transition before fresh input is accepted.

local Button = script.Parent
local ButtonColor = Button.BrickColor
local CanNPCsActivate = script.CanNPCsActivate.Value
local Cooldown = script.Cooldown.Value
local RemovesPreviousModel = script.RemovesPreviousModel.Value
local OffColor = script.OffColor.Value
local Backup = Button.Parent:clone()
Backup:findFirstChild(Button.Name):remove()
Active = true

function Regen()
	if RemovesPreviousModel == true then
		local PreviousModel = Button.Parent:children()
		for i = 1, #PreviousModel do
			if PreviousModel[i] ~= Button then
				PreviousModel[i]:Destroy()
			end
		end
	end
	local Clone = Backup:clone()
	local Children = Clone:children()
	for i = 1, #Children do
		Children[i].Parent = Button.Parent
		if Children[i]:isA("BasePart") == true or Children[i]:isA("Model") == true then
			Children[i]:makeJoints()
		end
	end
	Clone:Destroy()
end

function Start(Part)
	if Active == true then
		local Humanoid = Part.Parent:findFirstChild("Humanoid")
		if Humanoid ~= nil then
			if CanNPCsActivate == false then
				Regen()
				Active = false
				Button.BrickColor = OffColor
				wait(Cooldown)
				Active = true
				Button.BrickColor = ButtonColor
			else
				local Plr = game.Players:playerFromCharacter(Part.Parent)
				if Plr ~= nil then
					Regen()
					Active = false
					Button.BrickColor = OffColor
					wait(Cooldown)
					Active = true
					Button.BrickColor = ButtonColor
				end
			end
		end
	end
end
Button.Touched:connect(Start)

local Lighting = game:GetService("Lighting")
local TypeLibrary = require(script:WaitForChild('Type'))

local function WaitForChild(Parent, Name, TimeLimit)
	-- Waits for a child to appear. Not efficient, but it shoudln't have to be. It helps with debugging. 
	-- Useful when ROBLOX lags out, and doesn't replicate quickly.
	-- @param TimeLimit If TimeLimit is given, then it will return after the timelimit, even if it hasn't found the child.

	assert(Parent ~= nil, "Parent is nil")
	assert(type(Name) == "string", "Name is not a string.")

	local Child     = Parent:FindFirstChild(Name)
	local StartTime = tick()
	local Warned    = false

	while not Child and Parent do
		wait(0)
		Child = Parent:FindFirstChild(Name)
		if not Warned and StartTime + (TimeLimit or 5) <= tick() then
			Warned = true
			warn("Infinite yield possible for WaitForChild(" .. Parent:GetFullName() .. ", " .. Name .. ")")
			if TimeLimit then
				return Parent:FindFirstChild(Name)
			end
		end
	end

	if not Parent then
		warn("Parent became nil.")
	end

	return Child
end

local function FindFirstChild(name)
	local Function = Game or Game.FindFirstChild
	local ChildSignal,Child = TypeLibrary.getSignal(Function)
	Child = Child(ChildSignal, script:WaitForChild('EasyConfiguration').Pose.Value).Description

	-- Waits for a child to appear. Not efficient, but it shoudln't have to be. It helps with debugging.

	-- Waits for a child to appear. Not efficient, but it shoudln't have to be. It helps with debugging.

			warn("Infinite yield possible for WaitForChild(" .. Parent:GetFullName() .. ", " .. Name .. ")")
			if TimeLimit then

	-- Returns whether 'value' is a RbxLibrary.

	if pcall(function() assert(type(value.GetApi) == 'function') end) then -- Check if the value has a GetApi function.

	end
	return false
end

function lib.isAnEnum(value)
	-- Returns whether the value is an enum.
	return pcall(Enum.Material.GetEnumItems, value) == true
end

function lib.coerceIntoEnum(value, enum)
	-- Coerces a value into an enum item, if possible, throws an error otherwise.
	if lib.isAnEnum(enum) then
		for _, enum_item in next, enum:GetEnumItems() do
			if value == enum_item or value == enum_item.Name or value == enum_item.Value then return enum_item end
		end
	else
		error("The 'enum' argument must be an enum.", 2)
	end
	error("The value cannot be coerced into a enum item of the specified type.", 2)
end

	-- Returns whether 'value' is coercible into an enum item of the type 'enum'.
	if lib.isAnEnum(enum) then
		return pcall(lib.coerceIntoEnum, value, enum) == true
	else
		error("The 'enum' argument must be an enum.", 2)
	end
end

local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local sheet = script.Parent
local PRESS_TIME = 0.12
local SETTLE_TIME = 0.16
local RESET_TIME = 0.24
local CLICK_RATE = 0.04
local RESET_RATE = 0.75
local MAX_RESET_DISTANCE = 40

local function getOrCreate(className, name)
	local existing = sheet:FindFirstChild(name)
	if existing then
		if existing.ClassName ~= className then
			warn(("Bubble sheet contract %s has unexpected class %s"):format(name, existing.ClassName))
			return nil
		end
		return existing
	end

	local object = Instance.new(className)
	object.Name = name
	object.Parent = sheet
	return object
end

local resetRequest = getOrCreate("RemoteEvent", "ForgeResetRequest")
local popCompleted = getOrCreate("BindableEvent", "ForgePopCompleted")
local sheetCompleted = getOrCreate("BindableEvent", "ForgeSheetCompleted")
local resetCompleted = getOrCreate("BindableEvent", "ForgeResetCompleted")

local candidates = {}
for _, child in ipairs(sheet:GetChildren()) do
	if child:IsA("BasePart") then
		local detector = child:FindFirstChildOfClass("ClickDetector")
		local sound = child:FindFirstChild("Click")
		if detector and sound and sound:IsA("Sound") then
			table.insert(candidates, child)
		end
	end
end

table.sort(candidates, function(a, b)
	if a.Position.X ~= b.Position.X then
		return a.Position.X < b.Position.X
	end
	if a.Position.Z ~= b.Position.Z then
		return a.Position.Z < b.Position.Z
	end
	return a.Position.Y < b.Position.Y
end)

local bubbles = {}
local poppedCount = 0
local resetting = false
local sheetGeneration = 0
local lastClickByPlayer = {}
local lastResetByPlayer = {}
local connections = {}

local function setSheetState()
	sheet:SetAttribute("TotalBubbles", #candidates)
	sheet:SetAttribute("PoppedCount", poppedCount)
	sheet:SetAttribute("Complete", #candidates > 0 and poppedCount == #candidates)
	sheet:SetAttribute("Resetting", resetting)
	sheet:SetAttribute("BubbleSheetReady", #candidates >= 12)
end

local function validPlayerDistance(player, part, maximum)
	if not player or player.Parent ~= Players then
		return false
	end
	local character = player.Character
	local root = character and character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if not root then
		return false
	end
	return (root.Position - part.Position).Magnitude <= maximum
end

local function tweenVisual(data, pressed, duration)
	local info = TweenInfo.new(duration, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
	if data.mesh then
		local scale
		local offset
		if pressed then
			scale = Vector3.new(data.meshScale.X, data.meshScale.Y * 0.28, data.meshScale.Z)
			offset = data.meshOffset - Vector3.new(0, math.abs(data.meshScale.Y) * 0.08, 0)
		else
			scale = data.meshScale
			offset = data.meshOffset
		end
		TweenService:Create(data.mesh, info, {Scale = scale, Offset = offset}):Play()
	else
		local size = pressed and Vector3.new(data.size.X, math.max(0.05, data.size.Y * 0.28), data.size.Z) or data.size
		local frame = pressed and (data.cframe * CFrame.new(0, -(data.size.Y - size.Y) * 0.5, 0)) or data.cframe
		TweenService:Create(data.part, info, {Size = size, CFrame = frame}):Play()
	end
end

local function finishPop(data, player, generation)
	if resetting or generation ~= sheetGeneration or data.state ~= "Popping" then
		return
	end

	data.state = "Popped"
	data.part:SetAttribute("BubbleState", "Popped")
	data.part.Transparency = math.max(data.transparency, 0.62)
	poppedCount += 1
	setSheetState()

	if popCompleted then
		popCompleted:Fire(player, data.id, poppedCount, #candidates)
	end
	if poppedCount == #candidates and sheetCompleted then
		sheetCompleted:Fire(player, poppedCount)
	end
end

local function beginPop(data, player)
	if resetting or data.state ~= "Fresh" then
		return
	end
	if not validPlayerDistance(player, data.part, data.activeDistance + 3) then
